'''''Lithophyllum''''' is a genus of thalloid [[red algae]] belonging to the family [[Corallinaceae]].
[[File:Alga (Lithophyllum stictaeforme), Parque natural de la Arrábida, Portugal, 2020-07-23, DD 62.jpg|250px|thumb|''Lithophyllum stictaeforme''.]]
[[File: Lithophyllum_orbiculatum_037.jpg|thumb|250px|right|''L. orbiculatum'' on a rock fragment; rock length ~3 cm.]]
[[File:Lithophyllum okamurae - National Museum of Nature and Science, Tokyo - DSC07650.JPG|thumb|250px|right|''Lithophyllum okamurae'']]
[[File: Corallinaceae - Lithothamnium.JPG|thumb|240px|right|''Lithophyllum'' sp.]]

==Fossil record==
This genus is known in the fossil record from the [[Silurian]] to the [[Quaternary]] (from about 418.7 to 0.0 million years ago). Fossils of species within this genus have been found in Europe, United States, South America, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, India, Japan and Australia.<ref>[http://www.fossilworks.org/cgi-bin/bridge.pl?action=taxonInfo&is_real_user=1&taxon_no=54436 Paleobiology Database]</ref>

==Description==
The monomerous, crustose thalli are composed of a single system of filaments which grow close to the underlying surface. ''Lithophyllum'' reproduces by means of [[conceptacle]]s.  The [[epithallus]] is periodically shed to avoid organisms growing on top of the alga.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Johnson | first1 = C. | last2 = Mann | first2 = K. | title = The crustose coralline alga, ''Phymatolithon'' Foslie, inhibits the overgrowth of seaweeds without relying on herbivores | journal = Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology | volume = 96 | issue = 2 | pages = 127 | year = 1986 | doi = 10.1016/0022-0981(86)90238-8 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.algaebase.org/search/genus/detail/?genus_id=95 Description of ''Lithophyllum'' at AlgaeBase]</ref>
